notSetUp.heading: Not set up yet
notSetUp.what: This phone has not been set up as the shop's owner phone yet.
notSetUp.next: Make a new shop wallet with the Key app, or use setup text you already have.

setupSaved.heading: Owner phone set up
setupSaved.what: The setup is saved on this phone, sealed with a key that stays in the phone.
setupSaved.next: Keep the app open. It starts looking for the network now.

setupNotReadable.heading: Setup text not read
setupNotReadable.what: The setup text is not in the form this app reads, so nothing was saved.
setupNotReadable.next: Copy the setup text again from the key ceremony, then try again.

torAddressNotAccepted.heading: Tor address not accepted
torAddressNotAccepted.what: The address of Orbot must be a host, a colon and a port, like 127.0.0.1:9050.

torAlwaysOn.heading: Everything goes through Tor
torAlwaysOn.what: This app sends every connection through Tor, with Orbot, and has no way to turn that off.
torAlwaysOn.next: Check the address of Orbot below, and keep Orbot running.

orbotNotRunning.heading: Tor is not running
orbotNotRunning.what: This app sends everything through Tor, but Orbot is not running.
orbotNotRunning.next: Open Orbot and turn it on.

torBuiltIn.heading: Tor
torBuiltIn.what: This app runs Tor itself, so Orbot is not needed.
torBuiltIn.next: Nothing to do. To use Orbot instead, choose Use Orbot.

torUsesOrbot.heading: Tor through Orbot
torUsesOrbot.what: This app sends everything through Orbot, which must be installed and running.
torUsesOrbot.next: Keep Orbot running. To stop needing it, choose Built-in Tor.

torStarting.heading: Starting Tor
torStarting.what: This app is connecting to the Tor network, which can take up to a minute.

torFailed.heading: Tor did not start
torFailed.what: This app could not connect to the Tor network.
torFailed.next: Check that the phone is online, then try again. If it keeps failing, choose Use Orbot.

notANumber.heading: Check what you typed
notANumber.what: An amount, a number or a rate is empty or has something other than digits in it.
notANumber.next: Type whole numbers only, then try again.

counterNeeded.heading: Counter needed
counterNeeded.what: A refund is asked for on one counter's sale, and no counter is chosen.
counterNeeded.next: Choose the counter, or paste its identity of 64 digits, then try again.

counterNotAccepted.heading: Counter identity not read
counterNotAccepted.what: A counter's identity is exactly 64 digits and letters from a to f.
counterNotAccepted.next: Type the identity again, or choose the counter from the list.

responseNeeded.heading: Response needed
responseNeeded.what: The Key app's response is needed to finish the approval.
responseNeeded.next: Paste the response or choose its file, then press the button again.

responseNotReadable.heading: Response text not read
responseNotReadable.what: The text is not in the form this app reads, so the Key app's response was not used.
responseNotReadable.next: Copy the response again from the Key app, or choose its file instead.

requestReady.heading: Request ready
requestReady.what: The request for the Key app is ready, and nothing has been signed yet.
requestReady.next: Show it as a code, or save it as a file or copy it as text, give it to the Key app, then bring back its response.

requestCopied.heading: Request copied
requestCopied.what: The request is copied as text, written in lower case.
requestCopied.next: Paste it where the Key app can read it.

requestCodeAnimated.heading: Request shown as a code
requestCodeAnimated.what: The request is on the screen as a code that changes, one part after another.
requestCodeAnimated.next: On the Key app, choose Scan and point it at this code until it has read every part. Then press Done.

requestCodeStill.heading: Request shown as one code
requestCodeStill.what: The request is on the screen as one code that does not change.
requestCodeStill.next: On the Key app, choose Scan and point it at this code. Then press Done.

requestCodeNotMade.heading: No code could be made
requestCodeNotMade.what: The request could not be turned into a code, so nothing is shown.
requestCodeNotMade.next: Go back and save the request as a file, or copy it as text, instead.

scanCancelled.heading: Scan cancelled
scanCancelled.what: No code was read, so nothing was taken from the Key app.
scanCancelled.next: Scan the Key app's code again, or choose its file or paste its text instead.

scanNotAResponse.heading: Not the Key app's code
scanNotAResponse.what: The code read is not one the Key app shows for a response, so nothing was used.
scanNotAResponse.next: On the Key app, show the answer as a code, and scan that one.

counterReading.heading: Reading the counter
counterReading.what: The counter's request is being read and its four words worked out, which takes a moment.

counterNotACode.heading: Not a counter's code
counterNotACode.what: The code read is not one a counter shows for its request, so nothing was queued.
counterNotACode.next: On the counter, choose Pair and scan the code it shows.

counterScanCancelled.heading: Counter scan cancelled
counterScanCancelled.what: No code was read, so nothing was queued.
counterScanCancelled.next: Scan the counter's code again when you are ready.

counterCodeNotRequest.heading: Not a counter's request
counterCodeNotRequest.what: The code holds more than a counter's request can, so nothing was queued.
counterCodeNotRequest.next: On the counter, choose Pair and scan the code it shows.

sharesNote.heading: Equal shares
sharesNote.what: Each counter's share of the instant limit becomes 1/2.
sharesNote.next: Custom shares are set under Settings, in Change settings.

sharesNoteOne.heading: Equal shares
sharesNoteOne.what: This is the only counter, so its share of the instant limit is all of it.
sharesNoteOne.next: Custom shares are set under Settings, in Change settings.

counterCompare.heading: Compare the four words
counterCompare.what: Check that the counter shows these same four words, and that the Key app shows them too.
counterCompare.next: If they match, say so below. If they differ, say so and nothing is paired.

counterPriceNeeded.heading: Price needed
counterPriceNeeded.what: The starting limits are set in US dollars whatever money the shop takes, so this phone needs today's price of a bitcoin in US dollars.
counterPriceNeeded.next: Type today's price of one bitcoin in whole US dollars, then say the words match.

counterPriceFetching.heading: Getting today's price
counterPriceFetching.what: This phone is asking the price sources for the price of one bitcoin, through Tor.
counterPriceFetching.next: Wait a moment. If they do not answer, you can type the price.

counterPriceFetched.heading: Today's price
counterPriceFetched.what: The price sources give 98,500 US dollars for one bitcoin. The starting limits are worked out from it.
counterPriceFetched.next: If it looks right, say the words match. To use another price, type it below.

priceNotRead.heading: Price not read
priceNotRead.what: The price of a bitcoin is a whole number of dollars above 0, so nothing was queued.
priceNotRead.next: Type today's price of one bitcoin in whole dollars, like 98500.

counterCancelled.heading: Counter not added
counterCancelled.what: The four words did not match, so the counter's request was taken out of the queue.
counterCancelled.next: Start again on the counter, and scan the new code it shows.

counterNotPaired.heading: Counter not paired
counterNotPaired.what: The Key app did not approve this counter, so no code for it was made.
counterNotPaired.next: Read the words above, then scan the counter's code again to start over.

counterCodeAnimated.heading: Code for the counter
counterCodeAnimated.what: The code for the counter is on the screen in many parts, with its first addresses. Taking it takes about a minute.
counterCodeAnimated.next: Scan this with the counter and hold both phones steady. The counter counts the parts it has and shows Paired when it has them all.

counterCodeStill.heading: Code for the counter
counterCodeStill.what: The code for the counter is on the screen as one code that does not change.
counterCodeStill.next: Scan this with the counter. It shows Paired when it has taken it.

counterCodeNoBatch.heading: Code without addresses
counterCodeNoBatch.what: The first addresses are not in this code, because the link handed them over already.
counterCodeNoBatch.next: Scan this with the counter. It shows Paired when it has taken it.

counterCodeNotMade.heading: No code could be made
counterCodeNotMade.what: The code for the counter could not be made, so nothing is shown. What waits for the counter is kept.

counterDelivered.heading: Counter paired
counterDelivered.what: The counter shows Paired, so what waited for it is marked delivered.
counterDelivered.next: The counter takes its sales from its first addresses now.

ceremonyMakingKey.heading: Making key 1
ceremonyMakingKey.what: Key 1 is being made on this phone, which takes a moment.

ceremonyScanNext.heading: Scan the Key app
ceremonyScanNext.what: Open the Key app on the other phone and choose Set up keys.
ceremonyScanNext.next: Press the button below and scan the code it shows.

ceremonyNotAnAnswer.heading: Not the Key app's answer
ceremonyNotAnAnswer.what: The code read is not one the Key app shows for its answer, so nothing was used.
ceremonyNotAnAnswer.next: On the Key app, choose Set up keys, and scan the code it shows.

ceremonyCodeTooLong.heading: Code too long for an answer
ceremonyCodeTooLong.what: The code holds more than the Key app's answer can, so nothing was used.
ceremonyCodeTooLong.next: On the Key app, choose Set up keys, and scan the code it shows.

ceremonyScanCancelled.heading: Key app scan cancelled
ceremonyScanCancelled.what: No code was read, so no answer was taken from the Key app.
ceremonyScanCancelled.next: Scan the Key app's code again when you are ready.

ceremonyCompareRoot.heading: Compare the Key app's words
ceremonyCompareRoot.what: Check that the Key app shows these same four words as its own.
ceremonyCompareRoot.next: If they match, say so below. If they differ, say so and the answer is thrown away.

ceremonyRootDiffers.heading: Answer thrown away
ceremonyRootDiffers.what: The four words differ, so this answer may not come from the Key app you hold, and it was thrown away.
ceremonyRootDiffers.next: Scan again on the Key app you hold. If the words still differ, choose Start again.

ceremonyKey2Needed.heading: Key 2 needed
ceremonyKey2Needed.what: The Key app holds no key 2, so key 2 comes from the device that holds it.
ceremonyKey2Needed.next: Scan a key code from the other wallet app, or its key as text, or paste the text, then continue.

ceremonyKey2Text.heading: Key 2 text not accepted
ceremonyKey2Text.what: The text for key 2 is empty, is not text, or is longer than a key's text can be, so nothing was used.
ceremonyKey2Text.next: Copy it again from the device that holds key 2, then try again.

ceremonyKey2ScanCancelled.heading: Key 2 scan cancelled
ceremonyKey2ScanCancelled.what: No code was read, so key 2 was not taken.
ceremonyKey2ScanCancelled.next: Scan its code again, or paste its text instead.

ceremonyBuilding.heading: Building the wallet
ceremonyBuilding.what: The wallet is being built from the three keys, which takes a moment.

ceremonyCheckWallet.heading: Check the wallet
ceremonyCheckWallet.what: The checksum words and the fingerprints below are the wallet's. The Key app shows the same ones.
ceremonyCheckWallet.next: Show the Key app its setup next, and compare there.

ceremonyCodeAnimated.heading: Setup for the Key app
ceremonyCodeAnimated.what: The setup for the Key app is on the screen as a code that changes, one part after another.
ceremonyCodeAnimated.next: On the Key app, scan this code until it has read every part, then compare the words.

ceremonyCodeStill.heading: Setup for the Key app
ceremonyCodeStill.what: The setup for the Key app is on the screen as one code that does not change.
ceremonyCodeStill.next: On the Key app, scan this code, then compare the words.

ceremonyCodeNotMade.heading: No code could be made
ceremonyCodeNotMade.what: The setup for the Key app could not be turned into a code, so nothing is shown.
ceremonyCodeNotMade.next: Go back and try to show it again.

ceremonyCompareSetup.heading: Compare with the Key app
ceremonyCompareSetup.what: After it takes the setup, the Key app shows the checksum words and the fingerprints.
ceremonyCompareSetup.next: Check that they are the same as on this phone, then say so below.

ceremonyWordsDiffer.heading: Wallet not finished
ceremonyWordsDiffer.what: The words differ, so the wallet is not finished, and nothing should be paid to it.
ceremonyWordsDiffer.next: Choose Start again on both phones.

ceremonyScanAgain.heading: Scan the Key app again
ceremonyScanAgain.what: The wallet was built, but the setup for the Key app is not kept on this phone.
ceremonyScanAgain.next: Scan the Key app's code again to show the setup again.

ceremonyFinishing.heading: Finishing the setup
ceremonyFinishing.what: The setup is being finished and saved on this phone.

ceremonySaveNext.heading: Save the setup
ceremonySaveNext.what: The words were confirmed, but the setup was not saved on this phone yet.
ceremonySaveNext.next: Press the button below to save it and start.

ceremonyResume.heading: Setup in progress
ceremonyResume.what: A new shop wallet was started on this phone and is not finished.
ceremonyResume.next: Continue where it stopped, or start again.

ceremonyStartAgain.heading: Start again?
ceremonyStartAgain.what: The keys made so far are thrown away, and nothing has been paid to them.
ceremonyStartAgain.next: Choose Start again only if the Key app starts again too.

ceremonyThrownAway.heading: Started over
ceremonyThrownAway.what: The keys made so far were thrown away, and nothing was paid to them.
ceremonyThrownAway.next: Make a new shop wallet again, or use setup text you already have.

ceremonyRecordNotRead.heading: Setup record not read
ceremonyRecordNotRead.what: The record of the unfinished setup could not be read, so nothing was done.
ceremonyRecordNotRead.next: Choose Start again and make the wallet again. Nothing has been paid to it.

setupTextNeeded.heading: Setup text needed
setupTextNeeded.what: This phone takes the setup text of a key ceremony made elsewhere, pasted or from a file.
setupTextNeeded.next: Paste the setup text, or choose its file, then save.

watchSetting.heading: Watch in the background
watchSetting.what: The phone keeps following the shop's wallet while the app is closed, and tells the counters it is watching.
watchSetting.next: Turn it on to keep instant sales working. Android shows a notification while it runs.

watchNotificationsOff.heading: Notifications are off
watchNotificationsOff.what: Android needs to show a notification while the phone watches in the background, and notifications are off for this app.
watchNotificationsOff.next: Allow notifications for OpenBMT Owner in Android's settings, then turn this on again.

requestSaved.heading: Request saved
requestSaved.what: The request is saved as a file.
requestSaved.next: Carry the file to the Key app and open it there.

refundQueuedAtDepth.heading: Refund queued
refundQueuedAtDepth.what: The refund is in the queue, and the sale is deep enough to be refunded.
refundQueuedAtDepth.next: Bring this phone and the Key app together and start an approval.

refundQueuedWaiting.heading: Refund queued, sale new
refundQueuedWaiting.what: The refund is in the queue, but the sale is not deep enough yet to be refunded.
refundQueuedWaiting.next: Wait for more blocks. The refund can be approved when the sale is deep enough.

cashOutQueued.heading: Cash-out queued
cashOutQueued.what: The cash-out is in the queue and has not been sent for approval yet.
cashOutQueued.next: Bring this phone and the Key app together and start an approval.

cashOutPrice.heading: Today's price
cashOutPrice.what: The price sources give 98,500 dollars for one bitcoin. The books record this cash-out at that price.
cashOutPrice.next: If it looks right, go on. To use another price, type it below.

cashOutPriceNeeded.heading: Price needed
cashOutPriceNeeded.what: The price sources did not answer, and the books need what this cash-out is worth.
cashOutPriceNeeded.next: Type the price of one bitcoin, then go on.

booksEmpty.heading: No sales yet
booksEmpty.what: No counter has sent a sale to this phone yet.
booksEmpty.next: Nothing to do. Sales appear here as the counters report them.

booksSaved.heading: File saved
booksSaved.what: The accounting file is saved where you chose. Each line has a date, a sale number and an amount, and no addresses or payment IDs.
booksSaved.next: Give it to your bookkeeper. The full ledger also has the payment IDs.

ledgerSaved.heading: Full ledger saved
ledgerSaved.what: The full ledger is saved where you chose. It has each sale's payment IDs and value, so it shows the shop's payments on the blockchain.
ledgerSaved.next: Share it only with people you trust with that, such as your bookkeeper.

entryCancelled.heading: Entry cancelled
entryCancelled.what: The entry is taken out of the queue.

entryRequeued.heading: Entry queued again
entryRequeued.what: The entry that was sent back is in the queue again.
entryRequeued.next: Start an approval when the Key app is at hand.

sessionAbandoned.heading: Approval abandoned
sessionAbandoned.what: The open approval is closed, and its entries are back in the queue.
sessionAbandoned.next: Nothing to do. Start a new approval when the Key app is at hand.

abandonExported.heading: Already sent to the signer
abandonExported.what: This approval went to the signer, so it may already be signed and could still be sent.
abandonExported.next: If you abandon it, the payments go back in the queue and a new approval spends the same coins, so only one can ever be paid.

abandonedExported.heading: Back in the queue
abandonedExported.what: The payments are back in the queue. The payment sent to the signer is still watched: if it is sent, it counts as paid.
abandonedExported.next: Start a new approval when you are ready.

alertCleared.heading: Alert cleared
alertCleared.what: The alert is cleared from this phone.
alertCleared.next: Nothing to do. If the cause is still there, the alert comes back.

noteDismissed.heading: Note dismissed
noteDismissed.what: The note about a refund request is removed from the list.

noLink.heading: No link to the counters
noLink.what: This phone was set up without a relay, so no counter can report to it.
noLink.next: Nothing to do here. A setup text with a relay adds the link.

noSettingsYet.heading: No settings yet
noSettingsYet.what: The phone holds no settings for the shop yet, so there is nothing to show.
noSettingsYet.next: Nothing to do. They arrive with the first approval that carries settings.

editIntro.heading: Change the settings
editIntro.what: Pick a group, change what you need, then review. Nothing is queued until you press Queue the change.
editIntro.next: A change that loosens something needs the Key app. A stricter change does not.

editGroupCurrency.heading: Currency
editGroupCurrency.what: The money the counters price sales in, and the limits are set in.
editGroupCurrency.next: Choose one. Bitcoin Standard prices in sats and uses no price source.

editCurrencyRetype.heading: New currency, new limits
editCurrencyRetype.what: Every limit is set again in the new currency, so the change shows them empty.
editCurrencyRetype.next: Type each limit in the new currency, then review. The change needs the Key app.

editGroupInstant.heading: Instant sales
editGroupInstant.what: How much a counter may accept as paid before the payment is confirmed, for each way it checks.
editGroupInstant.next: Whole dollars. 0 turns a limit off.

editGroupPayments.heading: Payments
editGroupPayments.what: When a payment counts, how many blocks settle a sale, and the smallest bitcoin sale.
editGroupPayments.next: Change what you need, then press Done.

editGroupTips.heading: Tips
editGroupTips.what: Whether the counters ask the customer for a tip, and which tips they suggest.
editGroupTips.next: Turn tips on, and set up to three percents.

editGroupRefunds.heading: Refunds and overrides
editGroupRefunds.what: How much can be refunded, and how much cashiers and managers may accept against a red screen.
editGroupRefunds.next: Whole dollars. 0 turns a limit off.

editGroupSafety.heading: Safety
editGroupSafety.what: How recent this phone's report must be, and what the shop says about its network.
editGroupSafety.next: Change what you need, then press Done.

editGroupShares.heading: Counters' shares
editGroupShares.what: Each counter's share of every instant limit. The shares may add up to 100% at most.
editGroupShares.next: Type each share as a percent with up to two decimals.

editGroupLightning.heading: Lightning node
editGroupLightning.what: The shop's own Lightning node: every Lightning payment must be made out to this node's key.
editGroupLightning.next: Paste or scan the node's key or address, or remove the node.

editLightningNote.heading: Naming a node
editLightningNote.what: Naming a node needs the Key app, which shows the key in full.
editLightningNote.next: Afterwards, set up Lightning on each counter, which holds its own limited key.

editNothingChanged.heading: Nothing changed
editNothingChanged.what: Every value is what the settings hold now, so there is nothing to queue.
editNothingChanged.next: Go back and change a value, or leave the editor.

editNeedsKeyApp.heading: The Key app must approve
editNeedsKeyApp.what: Something here loosens a limit or a check, so the whole change needs the Key app's approval.
editNeedsKeyApp.next: Queue the change, then build the request for the Key app.

editTakesEffect.heading: Takes effect when delivered
editTakesEffect.what: Every change here makes things stricter, so this phone signs it alone and no approval is needed.
editTakesEffect.next: Queue the change. It takes effect when it is delivered to the counters.

editQueuedLoosening.heading: Change queued
editQueuedLoosening.what: The change waits for the Key app's approval. It takes effect after the Key app approves and it is delivered.
editQueuedLoosening.next: Build the request for the Key app, show it there, and bring its response back.

editQueuedTightening.heading: Change signed
editQueuedTightening.what: The change is signed by this phone and waits to be delivered to the counters.
editQueuedTightening.next: Nothing more is needed. See it under Waiting to be delivered.

editNodeNeeded.heading: Node key needed
editNodeNeeded.what: The node's key or address was left empty, so no node was named.
editNodeNeeded.next: Paste or scan the key or address of the node, or choose Remove the node.

editNoCounters.heading: No counters yet
editNoCounters.what: The settings list no counters, so there are no shares to change.
editNoCounters.next: Add a counter first. Equal shares are made when it is added.

editSharesNotPercent.heading: Share not accepted
editSharesNotPercent.what: A share must be a percent from 0 to 100, with up to two decimals, so nothing was saved.
editSharesNotPercent.next: Type each share again, like 50 or 33.33.

editTipNotRead.heading: Tip not accepted
editTipNotRead.what: A suggested tip must be a whole percent from 1 to 50, so nothing was saved.
editTipNotRead.next: Type it again, like 15, or leave it empty.

editValueNotReadDollars.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadDollars.what: The value for Refunds per day is not a whole number of dollars, so nothing was saved.
editValueNotReadDollars.next: Type whole dollars, like 25, or 0 to turn it off.

editValueNotReadPercent.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadPercent.what: The value for Underpayment still counted is not a percent, so nothing was saved.
editValueNotReadPercent.next: Type a percent with up to two decimals, like 0.5.

editValueNotReadBlocks.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadBlocks.what: The value for Blocks to settle a sale is not a whole number of blocks, so nothing was saved.
editValueNotReadBlocks.next: Type a whole number of blocks, like 6.

editValueNotReadMinutes.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadMinutes.what: The value for Heartbeat age for instant is not a whole number of minutes, so nothing was saved.

editValueNotReadSats.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadSats.what: The value for Smallest bitcoin sale is not a whole number of satoshis, so nothing was saved.
editValueNotReadSats.next: Type whole satoshis, like 1000, or 0 for none.

editValueNotReadSwitch.heading: Value not accepted
editValueNotReadSwitch.what: The value for Tor on the counters was not chosen, so nothing was saved.
editValueNotReadSwitch.next: Choose one of the two answers.

posNotConnected.heading: No till connected
posNotConnected.what: This phone is not reading any till, so no order is matched against the counters' sales.
posNotConnected.next: Choose the till's vendor, type its location, and paste a read-only sign-in, then connect.

posNeedsLink.heading: Till needs the link
posNeedsLink.what: Matching a till needs the link to the counters, and this phone was set up without a relay.
posNeedsLink.next: Nothing to do here. A setup text with a relay adds the link.

posTokenNotAccepted.heading: Sign-in not accepted
posTokenNotAccepted.what: A read-only sign-in is 1 to 512 letters, digits and signs, with no space in it.
posTokenNotAccepted.next: Paste it again from the till's system, or make a new one there.

posConnected.heading: Till connected
posConnected.what: The till is connected, and its sign-in is sealed on this phone and is not shown again.
posConnected.next: Nothing to do. Keep the app open: the till is read about once a minute.

posRemoved.heading: Till taken off
posRemoved.what: The till's settings, its sign-in and the matches kept for it are removed from this phone.
posRemoved.next: Nothing to do. Connect a till again when you want its orders matched.

posAcknowledged.heading: Alert acknowledged
posAcknowledged.what: The alert is acknowledged on this phone only: the Box and the counters do not learn of it.

posTokenMissing.heading: Sign-in missing
posTokenMissing.what: A till is connected, but this phone holds no sign-in for it, so nothing is read.
posTokenMissing.next: Replace the sign-in with a new read-only one from the till's system.

posAddressRefused.heading: Till address refused
posAddressRefused.what: The library asked for an address that is not the till's system, so nothing was sent.
posAddressRefused.next: Close the app and open it again. If it happens again, do not rely on the matching.

posPageTooLong.heading: Till answer too long
posPageTooLong.what: The till's system sent an answer longer than 8 megabytes, so it was not read.
posPageTooLong.next: Nothing to do now. The next read is in about a minute.

posReadCutOff.heading: Till read cut off
posReadCutOff.what: One read asked for more pages than a read may take, so it was ended.
posReadCutOff.next: Nothing to do now. The next read is in about a minute.

posNotReached.heading: Till not reached
posNotReached.what: The till's system did not answer through Tor, so nothing was read.
posNotReached.next: Check that the phone is online and Tor is connected. The next read is in about a minute.

starting.heading: Starting
starting.what: The owner node is starting and looking for the network.
starting.next: Wait a moment. Keep the app open.

stopped.heading: Owner node stopped
stopped.what: The owner node has stopped, so the wallet is no longer followed.
stopped.next: Close the app and open it again.

libraryMissing.heading: The app is incomplete
libraryMissing.what: The part of this app that runs the owner node did not load, so nothing was done.
libraryMissing.next: Do not use this copy. Install the app again from the place you got it.

fault.heading: Answer not readable
fault.what: The app could not read an answer from the owner node, so nothing was changed.
fault.next: Close the app and open it again. If it happens again, stop and do not spend.

storageUnavailable.heading: Phone storage not usable
storageUnavailable.what: The phone's protected storage did not start, so the saved setup was not opened.
storageUnavailable.next: Restart the phone and open this app again. If it happens again, stop and do not spend.

fileNotRead.heading: File not read
fileNotRead.what: The file could not be opened or read, so nothing was done.
fileNotRead.next: Pick the file again, or paste the text instead.

fileNotSaved.heading: Not saved
fileNotSaved.what: The app could not write to this phone's storage, so nothing was saved.
fileNotSaved.next: Try again. If it happens again, free some space on the phone.

choosePin.heading: Choose a PIN
choosePin.what: Key 1 on this phone is kept behind a PIN, which the app asks for every time it opens.
choosePin.next: Choose at least 6 digits, or a passphrase of at least 8 characters, and do not forget it.

upgradePin.heading: Set a PIN for key 1
upgradePin.what: Key 1 on this phone was saved without a PIN, so anyone who opens the app could use it.
upgradePin.next: Choose a PIN now; the setup is kept as it is and locked behind it.

unlockSetup.heading: Enter your PIN
unlockSetup.what: Key 1 on this phone is locked, so the app opens only with the PIN or passphrase.
unlockSetup.next: Type it and tap Unlock. Too many wrong tries wipe key 1 from this phone.

pinsDiffer.heading: The two PINs differ
pinsDiffer.what: The PIN typed the second time is not the same as the first, so nothing was set.
pinsDiffer.next: Type the same PIN in both fields, then try again.

pinChanged.heading: PIN changed
pinChanged.what: Key 1 on this phone is now locked behind the new PIN.
pinChanged.next: Nothing to do. Use the new PIN from now on.

working.heading: Working
working.what: The app is working with the PIN, which takes a moment.
working.next: Wait. Do not close the app.

waitForTry.heading: Wait before the next try
waitForTry.what: There were too many wrong tries, so the app waits before it takes another.
waitForTry.next: Wait for the time shown, then type the PIN again.

triesNotSaved.heading: Try not counted
triesNotSaved.what: The phone could not keep the count of wrong tries, so the PIN was not tried.
triesNotSaved.next: Try again. If it keeps failing, restart the phone and open this app again.

wiped.heading: Key 1 wiped from this phone
wiped.what: This phone's copy of key 1 was wiped after 10 wrong tries. The money is not lost: two of the three keys still exist.
wiped.next: Follow the recovery kit to move to a new wallet, or ask the person who holds key 2.

wipeFailed.heading: Wipe not finished
wipeFailed.what: Key 1 could not be wiped from this phone completely, so the app will try again when it opens.
wipeFailed.next: Close the app and open it again. If it keeps failing, uninstall the app.

cameraOff.heading: Camera is off for this app
cameraOff.what: This app is not allowed to use the camera, so it cannot scan a code.
cameraOff.next: Allow the camera for this app in the phone's settings, or paste the text or choose a file instead.

cameraNotStarted.heading: Camera did not start
cameraNotStarted.what: The camera could not be opened, so nothing was scanned.
cameraNotStarted.next: Close any other app that uses the camera and try again, or paste the text or choose a file instead.

editField_light_per_sale.heading: Light check: one sale
editField_light_per_sale.what: The largest sale accepted as instant when only a light check has seen the payment.

editField_light_budget.heading: Light check: all at once
editField_light_budget.what: The most that may wait for confirmation together across the shop, on a light check.

editField_node_per_sale.heading: Own node: one sale
editField_node_per_sale.what: The largest sale accepted as instant when the shop's own node has also seen the payment.

editField_node_budget.heading: Own node: all at once
editField_node_budget.what: The most that may wait for confirmation together across the shop, with the own node.

editField_box_per_sale.heading: Box only: one sale
editField_box_per_sale.what: The largest sale accepted as instant when only a Box reports the payment.

editField_box_budget.heading: Box only: all at once
editField_box_budget.what: The most that may wait for confirmation together across the shop, on a Box's word.

editField_underpayment_tolerance_bps.heading: Underpayment still counted
editField_underpayment_tolerance_bps.what: How far under the price a payment may fall and still count as paid.
editField_underpayment_tolerance_bps.next: A percent with up to two decimals, from 0 to 5.

editField_min_confirmations.heading: Blocks to settle a sale
editField_min_confirmations.what: How many blocks a payment needs before the sale counts as settled.

editField_final_confirmations.heading: Blocks until final
editField_final_confirmations.what: How many blocks until a sale is final and a refund may be paid. It is at least the number above.

editField_min_sale_sats.heading: Smallest bitcoin sale
editField_min_sale_sats.what: A bitcoin sale below this is turned away, because a tiny receipt can cost more to spend than it holds.
editField_min_sale_sats.next: Whole satoshis. 0 means no smallest sale.

editField_tips_on.heading: Ask for a tip
editField_tips_on.what: Whether the counters ask the customer for a tip, and which tips they suggest.
editField_tips_on.next: Turn tips on, and set up to three percents.

editField_tip_1.heading: First tip
editField_tip_1.what: Whether the counters ask the customer for a tip, and which tips they suggest.
editField_tip_1.next: A percent from 1 to 50, or empty.

editField_tip_2.heading: Second tip
editField_tip_2.what: Whether the counters ask the customer for a tip, and which tips they suggest.
editField_tip_2.next: A percent from 1 to 50, or empty.

editField_tip_3.heading: Third tip
editField_tip_3.what: Whether the counters ask the customer for a tip, and which tips they suggest.
editField_tip_3.next: A percent from 1 to 50, or empty.

editField_refund_cap.heading: Largest single refund
editField_refund_cap.what: The most one refund may pay back to a customer.

editField_refund_daily_cap.heading: Refunds per day
editField_refund_daily_cap.what: The most that may be refunded in one day, all refunds together.

editField_cashier_override_daily_cap.heading: Cashier's override per day
editField_cashier_override_daily_cap.what: The most one cashier may accept against a red screen in a day.

editField_manager_override_ceiling.heading: Manager's override ceiling
editField_manager_override_ceiling.what: The most a manager may accept against a red screen, over all their overrides.

editField_heartbeat_max_age_secs.heading: Heartbeat age for instant
editField_heartbeat_max_age_secs.what: How old this phone's last report may be before counters stop accepting instant sales.

editField_tor_on.heading: Tor on the counters
editField_tor_on.what: Whether the counters connect through Tor. Turning it off removes that protection.

editField_customer_wifi.heading: Customers can join the Wi-Fi
editField_customer_wifi.what: Whether customers can join the Wi-Fi a counter is on, or you are not sure. No removes a Tor requirement.
editField_customer_wifi.next: Choose Yes or unsure, or No.

boxAddressNotRead.heading: Address not read
boxAddressNotRead.what: The Box's address is host:port on your network, or a v3 .onion name and a port, so nothing was tried.

boxLooking.heading: Looking for the Box
boxLooking.what: The phone is asking the Box for its claim, which can take up to a minute.

boxPriceNeeded.heading: Price for the Box
boxPriceNeeded.what: The starting limits are set in US dollars whatever money the shop takes, so this phone needs today's price of a bitcoin in US dollars.
boxPriceNeeded.next: Type today's price of one bitcoin in whole US dollars, then queue the Box.

boxPriceFetching.heading: Getting today's price
boxPriceFetching.what: This phone is asking the price sources for the price of one bitcoin, through Tor.
boxPriceFetching.next: Wait a moment. If they do not answer, you can type the price.

boxPriceFetched.heading: Today's price
boxPriceFetched.what: The price sources give 98,500 US dollars for one bitcoin. The starting limits are worked out from it.
boxPriceFetched.next: If it looks right, say the words match. To use another price, type it below.

boxCompare.heading: Compare the four words
boxCompare.what: The Box shows four words on its own screen. They must be the same as these, and the Key app will show them too.
boxCompare.next: If they differ, go back. Nothing is paired until the Key app approves.

boxQueued.heading: Box queued
boxQueued.what: The Box's claim and the settings that add it wait for the Key app.
boxQueued.next: Build the request for the Key app, approve there, and bring its response back.

boxHanding.heading: Handing over the welcome
boxHanding.what: The Box is being given its welcome and the settings, which can take up to a minute.

boxHandoverKept.heading: The approval is kept
boxHandoverKept.what: The Key app's approval stays queued on this phone. Nothing was lost and the Box is not paired yet.
boxHandoverKept.next: Try again here once the Box answers. If the invitation ran out, make a new one on the Key app.

boxPaired.heading: Box paired
boxPaired.what: The Box took its welcome and this phone saved the link to it, with the counters the settings name.

boxLinkNotSaved.heading: Link not saved
boxLinkNotSaved.what: The Box took its welcome, but this phone could not save the link to it.
boxLinkNotSaved.next: Add the lines below to the setup text, then start the app again.

boxSavePin.heading: Save the link
boxSavePin.what: The Box took its welcome. The link to it is saved in the locked setup, so the PIN is needed to open it and lock it again.
boxSavePin.next: Type the PIN of this phone, then save the link.

boxForgotten.heading: Box forgotten
boxForgotten.what: The Box's claim and the settings that add it were taken out of the queue. The Box itself was not told.
boxForgotten.next: To add it again, make a new invitation on the Key app and connect the Box again.

UrWords.reading.heading: Reading the animated code
UrWords.reading.what: Reading the animated code: 3 of about 9 parts.
UrWords.reading.next: Keep the phone pointed at the code until it is done.

UrWords.restarted.heading: Code did not add up
UrWords.restarted.what: The parts read did not fit together, so reading starts again.
UrWords.restarted.next: Keep the phone pointed at the code. It reads from the first part again.

UrWords.otherCode.heading: Another code is in view
UrWords.otherCode.what: The code in view is not part of the one being read, so it is skipped.
UrWords.otherCode.next: Point the phone at the first code again, or cancel and start over.

UrWords.wrongKind.heading: Not the code expected
UrWords.wrongKind.what: This code carries something this step does not take, so nothing was used.
UrWords.wrongKind.next: Cancel, then ask for the right code again, or use a file instead.

UrWords.contentRefused.heading: Code content not usable
UrWords.contentRefused.what: The code was read in full, but what it holds is not in a form this step takes.
UrWords.contentRefused.next: Ask for the code to be shown again, or use a file instead.

UrWords.readerFailed.heading: Code reader failed
UrWords.readerFailed.what: The part of this app that reads codes gave no usable answer, so nothing was read.
UrWords.readerFailed.next: Close the app and open it again. If it happens again, use a file.

hardwareChooseTransport.heading: How to reach the signer
hardwareChooseTransport.what: The payment goes to the signer as moving codes on this screen or as a file, and the signed payment comes back the same way.
hardwareChooseTransport.next: Pick the one your signer uses. The names under each choice are examples.

hardwareSignerReview.heading: Check it on the signer
hardwareSignerReview.what: The signer's own screen is the second check. It shows each address, each amount and the fee.
hardwareSignerReview.next: Compare every address and amount with this screen. Approve on the signer only if they all match.

hardwareRegisterIntro.heading: Register the wallet
hardwareRegisterIntro.what: A signer signs for a wallet only after it has been shown the wallet.
hardwareRegisterIntro.next: Show the signer this code or file, then check the first address.

hardwarePartsMissing.heading: Keep scanning
hardwarePartsMissing.what: Some parts of the moving code have not been read yet. They can be read in any order.
hardwarePartsMissing.next: Hold the camera on the signer's screen until every part is read.

hardwareFirstAddressCompare.heading: Check the first address
hardwareFirstAddressCompare.what: On the signer, open its address list and find the first receive address.
hardwareFirstAddressCompare.next: Compare it with the address shown here, character by character.

hardwareFirstAddressDiffers.heading: Do not use with this signer
hardwareFirstAddressDiffers.what: The signer shows a different first address, so it holds a different wallet or was registered wrongly.
hardwareFirstAddressDiffers.next: Register the wallet again on the signer, then check again. If it still differs, do not take money into this wallet.

hardwareFirstAddressChecked.heading: First address checked
hardwareFirstAddressChecked.what: The signer shows the same first address as this phone, so it holds the same wallet.

hardwareFirstAddressSkipped.heading: First address not checked
hardwareFirstAddressSkipped.what: Nothing yet shows that the signer holds the same wallet as this phone.
hardwareFirstAddressSkipped.next: Check it from the wallet screen before the shop takes money.

hardwareReturnedNeeded.heading: Bring the payment back
hardwareReturnedNeeded.what: The signer has the payment. Its signature has to come back to this phone before the payment can be sent.
hardwareReturnedNeeded.next: Scan the code the signer shows, or open the file it saved. A payment the signer finished itself works too.

hardwareFileSaved.heading: File saved
hardwareFileSaved.what: The payment for the signer is in the file named below.
hardwareFileSaved.next: Put the file on the signer's memory card and sign it there. Then bring the signed file back.

ownSpendList.heading: Send from your wallet
ownSpendList.what: These refunds and cash-outs wait to be paid. They are paid from the shop's own wallet, which signs them.
ownSpendList.next: Pick the ones to send now, then tap Prepare.

ownSpendEmpty.heading: Nothing to send
ownSpendEmpty.what: No refund or cash-out is waiting to be paid from the shop's wallet.

ownSpendCompare.heading: What the wallet will show
ownSpendCompare.what: Each payment below is one transaction. The wallet shows each address, each amount and the fee.
ownSpendCompare.next: Keep this screen at hand. Approve in the wallet only if every line there matches these.

ownSpendTransport.heading: Give it to the wallet
ownSpendTransport.what: The payment goes to the wallet as moving codes on this screen or as a file. Nothing on this phone can sign it.
ownSpendTransport.next: Scan the code or open the file in the wallet, check every line, and sign there.

ownSpendReturn.heading: Bring the payment back
ownSpendReturn.what: The wallet has the payment. What it signed has to come back to this phone unless the wallet sent the payment itself.
ownSpendReturn.next: Scan the code the wallet shows, or open the file it saved. A payment the wallet finished works too.

ownSpendTaken.heading: Payment taken
ownSpendTaken.what: The signed payment matches the one prepared here, and it goes out to the network.
ownSpendTaken.next: Nothing to do. The queue shows it as paid once it is in a block.

ownSpendWaiting.heading: Waiting for the wallet
ownSpendWaiting.what: This payment was given to the wallet. If the wallet sends it itself, this phone sees it and marks it paid once it is in a block.
ownSpendWaiting.next: Bring back what the wallet signed, or do nothing if the wallet sent it.

ownSpendNotGiven.heading: Not given to the wallet
ownSpendNotGiven.what: This payment is prepared, but its file has not been given to the wallet yet.
ownSpendNotGiven.next: Open it and give the file to the wallet, or give it up to put it back in the queue.

ownSpendAbandoned.heading: Payment given up
ownSpendAbandoned.what: The prepared payment was given up, and its refunds and cash-outs are back in the queue.
ownSpendAbandoned.next: Nothing to do. If the wallet still sends the copy it signed, they are marked paid, and a new payment for them can never pay them twice.
